propositions: A git fetch connection that is established but transfers zero bytes hangs until the 300-second wall-clock timeout, wasting review time and risking review loss on repeated stalls.
The git argv is constructed without http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, so the curl handle lacks throughput-keyed abort and relies only on wall-clock timeout.
A legitimately slow but progressing fetch (e.g., 80 MB clone over 90 seconds) must not be aborted, requiring the abort to be keyed on throughput floor rather than wall time.
A transient low-speed abort should be retried in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal within a single review cycle, rather than deferring to a backfill pass.
The extracted git-subprocess and fetch-locking plumbing must be split from repo_snapshot.py into a new git_fetch.py module to satisfy the 800-LOC per-module size constraint.
